summary: Utah State fell 16-14 at Washington with Brosterhous making his first start. Utah is next. The defense kept the game close, but the offense needs designed runs that work and fewer possessions ending with the ball in opposing hands.

items.headline: Brosterhous started at Washington in place of Hillstead
items.tldr: Watch this week’s quarterback announcement before assuming the same starter for Utah.

items.headline: Seven of eight running-back carries failed to gain yards
items.tldr: Watch whether the blocks create a path for the backs. The offense needs dependable designed runs alongside the quarterback’s scrambles.

items.headline: Utah State allowed one touchdown at Washington
Utah beat Arkansas 43-10 before the rivalry game
items.tldr: Watch the quarterback both in the pocket and on keepers. Losing track of the back or tight end can turn containment into an open passing lane.

items.headline: Rice-Eccles scans tickets before security screening
items.tldr: Download your ticket into your phone’s wallet before arrival. Utah’s entry guide also points to no-bag lanes at the main gates.

lead.headline: Give the backs somewhere to go.
lead.body: Watch the designed runs before judging the offense by a scramble or a deep completion. Useful gains would make the next passing down less predictable.

matchup.question: What would give Utah State a chance at Utah?
matchup.answer: Create space for the running backs, protect the ball, and make the opposing quarterback finish drives through tight coverage.

signals.title: Run blocking
signals.detail: Watch whether the backs can get beyond the line of scrimmage without needing to escape a defender first.

signals.title: Defensive assignments
signals.detail: Watch the edge stay patient while the secondary follows its receivers. The quarterback must remain someone’s responsibility.

signals.title: Field position
signals.detail: Watch placement as well as distance. Pinning an opponent deep gives the defense more room to defend.
